title: Best Glean Alternatives for Enterprise Search Teams
summary: Glean alternatives differ in price, lock-in and control depth. Choose which trade-offs align with your enterprise search strategy.
body_markdown:
## Microsoft 365 Copilot


### Where Microsoft 365 Copilot fits


If your documents, mail and meetings already live in Microsoft 365, Copilot fits. It's weakest once the knowledge your teams need sits in other systems.


### Microsoft 365 Copilot pricing


You pay per user, per month, as an add-on on top of a qualifying Microsoft 365 plan. Microsoft's pricing page has the current rate and the list of eligible plans.


Roll it out to a whole company and you pay for the base licence and the add-on on every seat that uses it. That costs far more than rolling it out to the few teams that search all day.


So the seat count you choose sets the bill.


### Microsoft 365 Copilot strengths and limits


Inside Microsoft 365 the case is strong. Copilot searches SharePoint sites, OneDrive files, Outlook mail and Teams chats and meetings, and it works from the permissions those services already enforce.


That means you're not rebuilding access rules in a second system, and a person sees in answers only what they could already open.


Step outside Microsoft's own products and the limit shows up. Reaching a ticketing tool, a CRM or a code host means connectors, and each source depends on whether a connector exists and on someone configuring it.


Where a source has no connector, its content doesn't appear in answers. A company with half its knowledge outside Microsoft will get half-complete answers unless it does that connector work.


Lock-in is the third constraint, and it moves rather than disappears. Glean's dependency is on a search vendor. Copilot's dependency is on your productivity suite, because it only runs on a qualifying Microsoft plan.


Leaving Copilot later is easy, but leaving the licensing underneath it is not, so the switching cost is the whole Microsoft bill, not the add-on.


Copilot suits teams that already pay for Microsoft 365, keep most work inside it, and want one vendor and one permissions model. Teams whose sources are spread across many non-Microsoft tools will meet its search limit first.
